mechanics.body_shape: alias the receiver into ESI; call a two-instruction global accessor unconditionally; if its result is zero return 0; else load one 32-bit word from receiver + 0x80 and if it is zero return 0; else call 0x00ba6dc0 with ECX set to the ACCESSOR'S RETURN VALUE and the +0x80 word pushed as its single stack argument, and forward that call's EAX unchanged.
mechanics.control_flow: two conditional branches, both JZ, both targeting the single 0x00dd0570 arm: 0x00dd055a (on the accessor's result) and 0x00dd0564 (on the +0x80 word). One join, two exits, no loop. Both tests are plain TEST reg,reg with JZ, so JZ reads only ZF: neither is a signed nor an unsigned comparison, and a key whose top bit is set is NOT treated as negative.

receiver_displacement.0x80: the ONLY receiver displacement in the body, read once at 0x00dd055c (MOV EDX,dword ptr [ESI + 0x80]) and consumed as 0x00ba6dc0's single stack argument at 0x00dd0566. It is read as a VALUE, not as a pointer: the same word is TESTed against zero two instructions later, and the listing performs no load through it.

mechanics.central_fact: the receiver of 0x00ba6dc0 is NOT this body's receiver. 0x00dd0567 MOV ECX,EAX moves the FIRST call's return value -- the word at global 0x0167eae4 -- into ECX, so a third, unrelated object reaches 0x00ba6dc0 as 'this'. The decompilation's shape, FUN_00ba6dc0(*(int *)(param_1 + 0x80)), invites passing the receiver instead and is wrong; the model test attacks exactly this.
mechanics.read_ordering: the +0x80 word is read at 0x00dd055c, four instructions AFTER the accessor call at 0x00dd0553, so the read observes whatever the accessor left behind, not the value present at entry. The model test proves this by having its accessor observer rewrite the word on its way out.
mechanics.not_modelled: the callees' internals (0x00b3d2a0's global load and 0x00ba6dc0's table walk and its 0x00bbaa60 call) are other bodies' business; the try-level and exception machinery is absent here; the scratch register allocation below the argument surface is not observable through this ABI and is not claimed.

semantic_findings: The function is a two-guard forwarder. Its entire observable behaviour is: fetch a global manager pointer; refuse to proceed if it is null; read one 32-bit word from the receiver at +0x80; refuse to proceed if that word is zero; otherwise ask 0x00ba6dc0 to resolve that word against the global manager and hand the answer back verbatim.

The receiver of the second call is the global slot's value, NOT the receiver of this body (0x00dd0567 MOV ECX,EAX). This is the single highest-risk fact in the function: the decompilation's shape invites the opposite, and no other instruction in the 36 bytes supports it.

The +0x80 word is a packed index, INFERRED from 0x00ba6dc0's own body: it is masked to 0xffffff, split at bit 12 into a 5-stride row table and a 0xfff column, and its top byte is shifted out and passed as a third argument to 0x00bbaa60. This package deliberately does not put that reading into a member name, and the model test asserts no semantics for the word.

Both guards are TEST/JZ, so neither is a signed nor an unsigned comparison; a key in 0x80000000..0xffffffff is non-zero here and takes the live path. 0xffffffff is additionally 0x00ba6dc0's own -1 sentinel, which makes a signed reading of the guard doubly wrong.
The body performs no write of any kind. receiver.written_through is 0 and the listing has no store through ESI; the forwarded object is likewise never dereferenced here.

This body is a virtual method, reached only through vtable tables: zero direct callers, three DATA references. It performs no dispatch itself, so it is a leaf of the dispatch graph rather than a node in it.

The one global in the dependency chain, 0x0167eae4, is read by the callee 0x00b3d2a0 and not by this body. This body itself names no data-segment address, which is the evidenced absence the GLOBALS check reports.
unresolved_questions: What class owns this method? It is an entry in four vtable tables (0x0147ca30, 0x0147ca70, 0x0147caf8, 0x0147cc14) but this package's evidence does not attribute those tables to a class, and the Spore-ModAPI SDK tree is absent from this environment, so no header could be read. Every member and type name here is therefore spelled by address.

What is the receiver's +0x80 word? The body only loads it, tests it and pushes it. The packed-index reading is INFERRED from 0x00ba6dc0's body, not from this one, and its name, width semantics and valid range are unestablished.

What is the concrete type of the object 0x00b3d2a0 returns, and what does 0x00ba6dc0 do with its receiver's +0xc8? Both callees are modelled as black boxes here. pkg01-roots already leaves DAT_0167eae4's publisher and the returned manager's type open, and nothing here settles either.

Is the -1 sentinel at 0x00ba6dc5 reachable from this body? It is not, because this body's own guard diverts a null key and 0xffffffff is not null -- so a -1 key DOES reach 0x00ba6dc0 and gets its 0 back. Whether 0xffffffff is a meaningful value at +0x80 is unresolved.

Which of the four referencing tables is the live one for a given instance, and what is this method's slot index? Only the byte offsets read out of the tables are stated; the vtable header this package's evidence does not show would fix the index.

The ghidra_function.locals array claims three locals (param_1, iVar1, uVar2) and ghidra_parameter_count is 0 while the decompilation shows one parameter. The listing has no frame at all beyond the single saved ESI, so the machine record is preferred and the decompiler's locals are not modelled. What the decompiler's register allocation was tracking is not recoverable from this body.

RETURN SEMANTICS: the canonical claim is the string 'Word' and the source span declares 'Word', so the arm agrees -- but the agreement is between a SOURCE-SIDE SPELLING and a MACHINE-FIXED WIDTH, not between two machine observations. abi_derived.value.abi.return_semantics is the register-class phrase `integral_in_EAX` and abi_derived.return.type is null, so no record for this VA supplies a C type, and a width-based oracle could not adjudicate this body in any case: the last value-producing instruction before both terminators is 0x00dd0569 CALL 0x00ba6dc0, and a CALL inside the body defeats evidence_returns' WIDTH state by design, because whether a caller may read EAX after a call is the CALLEE's signature and this listing cannot show it. So the residual question is exactly the one the record leaves open: which of the integral types of that four-byte word the original was written as. `Word` is one honest spelling and not a recovery -- a 32-bit pointer, a handle and a count are all 4 bytes and all `integral` in EAX, and the callee's own return is INFERRED (see return_semantics.value_meaning) to be a planet-record-shaped pointer without this body establishing that. Nothing here distinguishes them, and the declaration does not claim to.

validation.wpedantic_note: This package is not -Wpedantic-clean on GCC, and the cause is the prescribed calling-convention macro pattern itself rather than anything in the reconstruction: PKG_SWARMW1_00DD0550_THISCALL expands to __attribute__((thiscall)) on a free function, and GCC reports 'thiscall attribute is used for non-class method' three times (the two declarations in the header at 0x00ba6dc0 and 0x00dd0550, and the definition in the .cpp). The attribute is applied because the machine fixes the convention -- ECX receiver plus a callee-popped stack word for 0x00ba6dc0, fixed by its own MOV ESI,[ESP+0x8] and RET 0x4 -- and a free function is the only way to express a thiscall outside a class without inventing a class the evidence does not establish. The gate the worker contract specifies, -Wall -Wextra -Werror, is clean. The reference package that reached STATIC PASS records the identical limitation, so this is a known and accepted property of the convention macro, not a defect introduced here.

RETURN SEMANTICS was reported WARN ('return type differs or is semantically renamed; review required') and that blocker is REMOVED. The WARN came from the string-agreement arm, which owns a target exactly when a canonical return_type exists in abi_sources; this sidecar published observed_original_abi.return_type 'uint32' while the source span declares 'Word' (the package header's alias for std::uint32_t), so the two could never compare equal. The repair was sidecar-only and is a spelling fix, not a semantic one: observed_original_abi.return_type is now 'Word', the machine's own register-class phrase `integral_in_EAX` moved verbatim out of the type field into the sibling field machine_return_semantics, and the width-versus-spelling argument is recorded in observed_original_abi.return_note. Not one byte of the reconstruction changed, no model-test assertion was touched, and the model test still exits 0. What the repair does NOT do is settle the type: the machine fixes one four-byte unsigned integral word in EAX, and the C spelling of that word remains this package's choice -- see unresolved_questions.
